El primer «examen» de una inteligencia a: The first “exam” for an artificial intelligence was proposed by Alan Turing in 1950: a written conversation in which a judge had to decide whether they were talking to a person or to a machine. This exam is more modest and more honest: it does not ask whether a model seems clever, but whether whoever is studying it can do the sums that make it work.

Un examen de bloque es un simulacro hech: A block exam is a mock done at home: with a clock, no notes and no hints. The questions come from the exercises of the block's 12 topics, spread across sections, and each time you start one the numbers are different and so are the topics: doing it several times covers the whole block. On submitting, everything is marked, the step-by-step solution to each question opens and the mark comes out by section, with links to what is worth revising. The “tailored to what you have done” option puts first what you have not yet solved: it is the way to check that no topic is left untouched.
